title: Man in the Car Paradox
coreMove: Notice when a purchase is asking strangers to admire you and redirect the money toward a value you can actually feel.
sourcePressure: Status objects often make observers imagine themselves in the object rather than admire the owner.
chapterSpecificMisunderstanding: Treating this as a simple warning against nice things.

exampleSpecs.domain: a watch collector realizing nobody at the conference notices who owns the rare model
exampleSpecs.audience: a professional tempted to buy admiration through scarcity
exampleSpecs.stakes: the purchase may produce envy for the object, not respect for him

exampleSpecs.domain: a wedding planner steering a couple away from a dramatic entrance designed for social media
exampleSpecs.audience: a couple confusing public spectacle with being cherished

exampleSpecs.domain: a home renovator choosing between a visible marble foyer and quiet soundproofing

exampleSpecs.domain: a high school senior buying designer sneakers for the first week of class
exampleSpecs.audience: a teen learning the gap between being noticed and being admired
exampleSpecs.stakes: the purchase may amplify self-consciousness rather than belonging

exampleSpecs.domain: a chef plating for critics instead of regular diners

exampleSpecs.domain: a nonprofit donor wanting a public wall plaque for a gift
